topic: 2026 project scale-up: Samsung E&A EPC agreement
wiki_text: In July 2026, developer URSUS Energy announced an engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) framework agreement with Samsung E&A for the Coatzacoalcos (PODEBIS) LNG export project, scaling the plan up to a targeted 2.1 million tonnes per year (mtpa) of capacity and a total investment of roughly US$2.1 billion -- of which the previously-announced US$450 million Bancomext-financed figure represents only the initial phase. Civil works were reported as planned to begin in summer 2026, with first export targeted for late 2029. The same announcement referenced an unresolved port-concession dispute with a prior concessionaire, Mota-Engil, at the project site, which the reporting outlet said could complicate execution. Note: a second independent outlet's headline cited a total of US$2.2bn for the same announcement, a figure this batch could not fully reconcile with the US$2.1bn figure (see qa note).

wiki_text: In mid-2026, New Fortress Energy Inc (NFE), the 100% owner/operator of all five Altamira FLNG units, undertook a corporate debt restructuring involving an English Court scheme of arrangement and recognition under US Chapter 15, reported in trade press as splitting the company's assets between a 'BrazilCo' and a 'CoreCo.' NFE's own statements described this as producing an expected 'change in ownership/control' at the stake/creditor level of its Mexico LNG holdings. Based on available reporting, the entity GEM tracks as Owner/Operator ('New Fortress Energy Inc') continues to exist and to directly hold the Altamira asset through this process; no evidence was found this batch that the project-level legal entity itself changed. This is recorded here as background context on an evolving corporate situation, not as a confirmed GEM Owner/Parent field change (see qa note; re-check once the restructuring finalizes).
